title: Submodular Inference of Diffusion Networks from Multiple Trees
review_status: full-text audit complete; submodular objective, synthetic/real data setup, comparison outcomes, scalability test and fixed-network assumption checked
sections_checked: Submodular objective and greedy inference method
Synthetic network topologies and cascade-count experiments
evidence_note: Often higher recall than NetInf for small cascade counts; advantage narrows as cascades increase and NetRate wins on one hierarchical synthetic graph. Real evaluation defines reference edges by hyperlinks among top 1,000 sites, not observed causal influence. Model assumes fixed network. 100K/200K-node synthetic runs with 10K cascades report 10.12/12.14 ms per added edge.

title: Faster Private Release of Marginals on Small Databases
review_status: full-text audit complete; differential-privacy model, adaptive-query accuracy, database-size/running-time conditions, polynomial lower bound and practical considerations checked
sections_checked: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 query and offline guarantees
Polynomial representation approach and lower bound
Practical considerations, related work and future directions
evidence_note: (ε,δ)-DP online release; adaptively chosen k-way marginals receive additive ±0.01 error with probability ≥0.99 under n≥C d^0.51 log(|Q|)log(1/δ)/ε, with polynomial-in-n and subexponential-in-d per-query runtime. Practical multiplicative-weights evidence and alternative database regimes are discussed in the paper. Polynomial lower bound applies to the low-weight polynomial method, not all DP mechanisms.

title: Sparse similarity-preserving hashing
review_status: full-text audit complete; sparse encoder, CIFAR-10/NUS protocols, retrieval quality and latency tradeoffs, cross-modal results, version chronology checked
sections_checked: CIFAR-10 and NUS-WIDE data splits and similarity labels
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submission 2013-12-19; checked v3 dated 2014-02-16; venue not independently checked
evidence_note: SparseHash reports higher recall at similar precision than dense codes with comparable degrees of freedom; 128-bit CIFAR codes average about 6% sparsity. However, its own CIFAR speed test finds lookup faster at Hamming radius 0-1 and brute force faster at radius 2. Similarity labels are shared classes/concepts; CIFAR uses 200 training images per class and NUS uses 100K training pairs.
